transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Mark Bennett (Ridgeway Head of ML), Alison Chu (Infra), Rajesh Nair (Security), Tina Lopez (Product)

Summary: quick discovery focused on dedicated / reserved capacity. Customer is evaluating tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, strong security and isolation needs, wants predictable throughput for peak trading hours and occasional bursts. Discussed sizing, burst strategy, fallback to hosted, KMS, SOC2 and audit logs. Agreed next steps to share pricing, sizing spreadsheet, and schedule a deeper technical benchmark.

Topics: Dedicated sizing, isolation (VPC / tenant), burst and autoscaling policies, QoS and latency SLOs, KV cache / batching impacts, encryption/KMS, compliance requirements, rollout strategy and pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for blocking time. I'm Samira from Redwood, and with me is Diego from our systems engineering team. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Mark: Hi, doing good, Mark here. Thanks for taking the time. We're excited to dig in, we've been evaluating options for dedicated capacity for some of our inference workloads.
[00:12] Alison: Yep, Alison from infra. We primarily care about isolation and predictable throughput for market-hours traffic.
[00:18] Diego: Great, thanks. Quick agenda — we wanted to understand your current load, constraints, security needs, and talk through how Redwood Dedicated would fit — reserved GPUs, autoscaling/burst, and options for private deployments.
[00:28] Tina: Sounds good. I'll note that product also wants predictable latency for sequences up to 2k tokens, and occasional spikes when new features ship.
[00:36] Rajesh: From security: SOC2 is a given, and we need KMS integration and audit logs, plus SSO. Also curious about data residency — some of our customers are EU-only.
[00:44] Samira: All that makes sense. Quick qualification: are you running models in-house today or using hosted APIs?
[00:49] Mark: Right now we use a mix. Low-critical experiments on hosted APIs, some in-house sparse clusters but nothing in prod. Cost's a big factor — we want to avoid overprovisioning but need isolation for certain cohorts.
[00:59] Diego: Understood. For Dedicated, you reserve GPU pools which gives isolation and predictable throughput. You can configure autoscale policies and burst capacity. The tradeoff is commit vs on-demand. Can I ask about your typical and peak QPS and average sequence length?
[01:12] Mark: Typical baseline is ~10 QPS per model during off-hours, peaks up to 250 QPS across regions during market open, with tail spikes to ~400 for a few minutes when batch jobs overlap. Sequences usually between 256-1k tokens, some feature experiments hit 2k.
[01:28] Diego: That's helpful. Mm. For that profile, we'd look at several reserved nodes with headroom for burst. Our Dedicated autoscaler can maintain a steady pool for baseline and permit short-term burst via reserved spare capacity or configured burst credits — or fall back to our Hosted layer if you enable cross-tier fallback.
[01:43] Alison: Can you explain the fall back to Hosted? For compliance reasons, some data can't leave our VPC. Is fallback only for non-sensitive traffic?
[01:50] Samira: Good question. Fallback is policy-driven. You can set routing rules by tag or route so sensitive requests always stay in Dedicated/Private. For non-sensitive traffic, you can allow fallback to Hosted to reduce tail latency if Dedicated is temporarily saturated. We recommend defaulting to Dedicated for regulated datasets.
[02:06] Rajesh: On KMS — do you integrate with customers' KMS or require Redwood-managed keys? We need HSM-backed keys for certain payment data.
[02:13] Diego: We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can integrate with HSM in Private deployments. For Dedicated we offer either customer KMS attachments for model encryption and audit logs.
[02:22] Mark: Great. Also, how do you handle KV cache and batching? Our models use long context and we care about latency.
[02:28] Diego: The runtime supports KV cache for long contexts; we maintain per-session KV to avoid recomputing prefixes. For latency-sensitive calls, we use continuous batching tuned to target latency SLOs. There's also an intelligent batching engine that groups similar-length sequences to avoid token-padding waste. For your 256-2k spread, we'd recommend workload-aware batching profiles — Diego: we can show sample profiles in the deep dive.
[02:50] Mark: Is there an ops surface for this? We need to see per-token cost, latency per model, and tracing.
[02:56] Samira: Yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-route latency breakdown, and tracing hooks. You can export logs to your SIEM and we keep audit trails.
[03:05] Alison: On the networking front, we need VPC peering and egress controls. Is Dedicated in our VPC or do you host it?
[03:12] Diego: There are two deployment patterns. Dedicated can be run in a customer VPC (private deployment) or in a Redwood-managed environment with VPC peering and strict network controls. For the strictest isolation you can choose Private (on-prem or VPC-hosted) where control plane is still separated.
[03:26] Rajesh: And what about maintenance windows and model rollouts — can we manage model versions and do canary rollouts?
[03:33] Samira: Yes, the platform supports version pinning, canary and A/B rollouts, automatic fallback policies and metrics-based rollbacks. You can configure thresholds for request latency or error rate to trigger rollback.
[03:44] Tina: Pricing — how are bursts billed? If we reserve some capacity and then burst to hosted, how's that invoiced?
[03:51] Samira: Billing is split: reserved capacity is a committed monthly charge; burst to Hosted is pay-as-you-go usage, and any dedicated overage above reserved pool is billed at an overage rate. We can provide a sample pricing sheet and run scenarios once we have your QPS/sequence data.
[04:06] Mark: Does Redwood do any auto-quantization to reduce GPU memory and cost?
[04:11] Diego: We support quantized execution paths and recommend quantization profiles per model. We can do model-suggested quantization and test to ensure quality doesn't degrade. Redwood Optimize provides recommendations based on your workload.
[04:22] Mark: For the pilot, we want to run 2-4 models on dedicated capacity for 2 weeks and compare latency and cost to our current infra. Can Redwood help run that benchmark?
[04:31] Samira: Absolutely. Typical pilot is 2 weeks — we provide a sizing template and runbook. Diego will set up a benchmark plan including target prompts, sequences, and metrics.
[04:39] Diego: We'll need sample prompts, a target SLA per model, and a representative traffic curve. Also permission to synthetic-traffic test the Dedicated pool to validate burst behavior.
[04:49] Alison: Regarding autoscaling, how quick is scale-up? If we see a spike to 400 QPS, will the system spin up nodes fast enough?
[04:56] Diego: Scale-up depends on whether the autoscaler uses cold starts or reserved burst capacity. For true instant scaling we recommend keeping a small buffer of warm GPUs in the pool or enabling quick-burst credits — basically pre-warmed capacity. Cold node provisioning can take minutes; warm capacity provides sub-10s scale.
[05:12] Rajesh: What's the minimum commit for Dedicated? We want to avoid large long-term commitments before we see results.
[05:18] Samira: Minimums vary by region and GPU type, but we commonly start with a 3-month pilot with modest reserved capacity. For enterprise contracts we do annual reserved capacity at discounted rates. For pilots we can do month-to-month reserved pools.
[05:31] Tina: Any limitations on model types or custom models? We run a mix of Llama-family and some proprietary transformer variants.
[05:37] Diego: We onboard custom models — runtime supports common archs and we do model-validation tests. For custom kernels or unusual ops we might need extra engineering time. We'll need to run a quick compatibility check.
[05:47] Mark: On observability, can we stream logs to our Splunk/Datadog?
[05:51] Samira: Yes, logs and metrics can be exported to your observability stack and we provide tracing hooks and per-request IDs.
[05:57] Rajesh: For compliance, we need retention controls and ability to purge data. Is that available?
[06:02] Diego: Yes — retention policies, query-level purge, and audit logs are supported. For regulated data, Private deployments give you the strongest guarantees.
[06:10] Mark: Are there any known multi-tenancy risks with Dedicated? I mean, if you're running dedicated pools for multiple customers on same infra, how isolated is it?
[06:18] Diego: Dedicated means isolated GPU pools and tenant-level separation. Network and storage isolation is enforced. For the highest assurance we offer Private deployments where the control plane runs in your VPC or on-prem, eliminating cross-tenant blast radius.
[06:29] Tina: Implementation timeline — how long to get Dedicated up for a pilot?
[06:33] Samira: Usually 2-4 weeks to provision and validate a pilot environment, less if we use Redwood-managed Dedicated with VPC peering; longer if on-prem / air-gapped.
[06:43] Mark: Ok, good. One follow up — for peak hours, how would you recommend mixing SLOs vs cost? If we keep too many warm GPUs we waste cost, but if we keep too few we risk latency.
[06:54] Diego: Common pattern: keep baseline pool for typical QPS and use short-term burst credits to cover 95th-99th percentile. For extreme tails, route lower-priority traffic to Hosted or lower-cost quantized model variants. Also use KV cache and prefix caching to reduce compute for repeated queries.
[07:10] Alison: Are there tools for simulating traffic patterns to choose the right reserve?
[07:14] Diego: Yes, Redwood provides a sizing template and simulation harness. We'll run simulations using your historical qps curve to estimate reserve size and cost. We'll include sensitivity analysis for different spike durations.
[07:24] Mark: On security docs — can you send SOC2, penetration test summaries, and architecture compliance docs?
[07:29] Samira: Yes, we'll share our security pack and SOC2 report. For Private we can provide extra detail.
[07:36] Rajesh: One more on SSO — we use Okta with SAML.
[07:40] Diego: We support SAML SSO, RBAC, and fine-grained roles.
[07:44] Tina: Any concerns about model updates breaking performance? We want to do canary tests and rollback if quality regresses.
[07:50] Samira: Redwood Optimize runs quality regression checks tied to prompt sets; you can set alerts for regressions and automatically rollback.
[07:57] Mark: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[07:59] Samira: Recap: we'll send pricing and sizing spreadsheet, security docs including SOC2 and KMS integration docs. Diego will schedule a throughput/kvcache deep dive and set up the benchmark kickoff. Ridgeway will share QPS/latency dashboards and example prompt set. Action owners as noted.
[08:17] Mark: That works. Thanks — we'll review and get the materials out early next week.
[08:21] Samira: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the doc pack and proposed times for the deep dive.
[08:26] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions around kernel names and some product names; speaker overlaps at times.
